newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi radio says 42 people killed in church.
newsitem.headline: Burundi radio says 42 people killed in church.

text.p: Forty-two people were killed in a church south of Burundi's capital, state radio said on Monday. The army said it had no information on the reported killings.

The 42 were said in the obituaries section of a broadcast on the radio to have been Pentecostalists killed on May 14 in a church at Rutenba hill in Muhuta commune, 27 km (17 miles) south of Bujumbura.
Army spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Isaie Nibizi said he had no information on the reported killings, which included men and women. Most of the dead were members of Burundi's Hutu majority.
More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebels since Burundi's first elected Hutu president was assassinated by troops in 1993.

Earlier on Monday, military sources in the northwestern province of Cibitoke said the army had killed 30 Hutu rebels and captured 15 following a clash with rebels, former Rwandan and Zairean soldiers and Rwandan Hutu militiamen last week.
They added that fighting continued in Mabayi, Mogina and Mogwi communes, northwest of Bujumbura.

The military sources said top officers of the armies of Burundi and Rwanda met at the weekend and the Rwandan army said Interahamwe militiamen and former soldiers planned to enter the Nyungwe forest from where they would intensify their campaign.
The Rwandans said the former soldiers hid their weapons in the forest as they fled Rwanda in 1994 after the genocide of 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus, according to the Burundi military sources.
"(Hutu) rebels are circling around Cibitoke and it is hard to say whether these attacks will end," an army officer said.
"Rebels move around like water in the ocean. You hit one area and find they have already moved to the next," he added.
The U.N. refugee agency estimates that some 100,000 people have been displaced by the fighting in the Cibitoke province.

Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army arrested 14 students last Wednesday during a university sit-in protest against President Pierre Buyoya's decision to negotiate with the Hutu rebels. The two sides signed a pre-ceasefire agreement in March after secret talks in Rome.
